applied.problem: "Every check looks better" overreaches: leaving out the vertical runs flatters the drop and Zs, but it raises the worked fault current, so the heat check comes out harder, not easier (lesson 7's 5.00 mm² against 4.44 mm² here).

The Cmax heat checks use the hot (×1.28) resistances; with the cooler conductors a lightly loaded circuit really has, more current flows, and at the DBL2 end C7's 1.5 mm² cpc no longer passes at 0.1 s, so the "slim pass" needs that caveat.

Screen 6's slip says "The conductors are hot when the fault comes", but the submain carries 8.22 A on a cable rated 44 A; the multiplier is the design taking them at their full working heat, not a fact about every fault.

"A heavy load runs out of voltage first" is stated as a rule; with a tighter device (a type C on a bigger cable, say) Zs can still run out first, so it needs the same "usually" as the light-load line and the explanation.
